answer: Because shards cannot be shared: the beacon hands each wallet one unique erasure-coded fragment of the epoch archive, and a falcon probe may summon that fragment for re-derivation seconds later. A clone farm built on one kernel answers with one machine's latency and collides on demand; to split custody honestly, every ghost must keep its own live node paying real storage in the tundra. Duplicating a wallet is cheap; duplicating distinct, retrievable memory never is.
